key_insight: Adding time as an explicit dimension of interpretability makes differentiable decision trees more understandable for sequential decision-making, especially when combined with action chunking.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical way to deploy transparent policies for safe autonomy that remain compact, differentiable, and competitive with neural networks.
method: Introduced two policy-gradient algorithms for action-chunked differentiable decision trees.
Added an information-theoretic tree restructuring method to keep trees parameter-efficient during training.
Showed that warm-starting from a distilled action-chunked policy yields the best temporal interpretability.
evidence_signal: Across four simulation environments, the proposed approach matched neural network performance in three domains while using up to 80% fewer parameters.
watch_item: The strongest results depend on warm-starting and action chunking, so performance and interpretability may be sensitive to the quality of the distilled initialization and chunk design.
